facts.statement: Blikanasaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived during the late Triassic in South Africa.
facts.quote: Blikanasaurus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the late Triassic of South Africa.

facts.statement: The genus name Blikanasaurus means "lizard from Blikana" in Greek.
facts.quote: The generic name Blikanasaurus is derived from Greek, meaning "lizard from Blikana".

facts.statement: The species name cromptoni honors American paleontologist A.W. "Fuzz" Crompton, who led expeditions in the Elliot Formation.
facts.quote: The species name cromptoni is taken from the surname of A.W. "Fuzz" Crompton, an American paleontologist who led numerous field expeditions in Elliot Formation outcrop localities in South Africa.

facts.statement: Blikanasaurus is known only from partial hindlimb bones found in the lower Elliot Formation in the Eastern Cape.
facts.quote: Blikanasaurus is only known from partial hindlimb bones that were recovered from the lower Elliot Formation (LEF) in the Eastern Cape.

facts.statement: The first Blikanasaurus fossils were found at the foot of Blikana mountain in Herschel, Eastern Cape, South Africa.
facts.quote: Blikanasaurus was first discovered by a partial hindlimb (epipodium and pes) found in the lower Elliot Formation (LEF) at the foot of Blikana mountain in Herschel, Eastern Cape of South Africa in .

facts.statement: A second specimen, consisting of a right metatarsal, was recovered in the early 2000s from the Damplaats farm in the eastern Free State.
facts.quote: In the early 2000s, a second specimen - consisting of only a right metatarsal - was recovered from lower Elliot Formation deposits on the farm, Damplaats, in Ladybrand of the eastern Free State.

facts.statement: A recently found possible ilium has been attributed to Blikanasaurus, but this attribution remains unconfirmed.
facts.quote: A possible ilium that has been attributed to Blikanasaurus was found recently, although its attribution to Blikanasaurus remains to be confirmed.

facts.statement: Blikanasaurus is known to have heavily built hindlimb bones.
facts.quote: The only information that has been deduced is from the bones of its hindlimb anatomy, which are heavily built.

facts.statement: Blikanasaurus possessed unusually thick ankles and large phalanges.
facts.quote: Los tobillos son inusualmente gruesos y las falanges grandes.

facts.statement: Blikanasaurus is estimated to have been between three and five meters long.
facts.quote: Habría tenido de tres a cinco metros de largo.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that Blikanasaurus was an obligate quadruped due to its robust build.
facts.quote: Due to its robust build, Blikanasaurus is hypothesized to have been an obligate quadruped, unlike what is characteristic of more basal sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: Blikanasaurus is currently classified as a basal sauropodomorph, though little is known due to incomplete fossils.
facts.quote: Blikanasaurus is now considered to be a basal sauropodomorph; however, due to the lack of complete specimens, little remains known about this enigmatic taxon.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists proposed grouping Blikanasaurus in the family Blikanasauridae, but this family has not been formally accepted.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists claimed a case to group Blikanasaurus within the family Blikanasauridae, a family named by Galton and van Heerden in 1985, however, this family has not been formally accepted due to it lacking definitive taxa.

facts.statement: Blikanasaurus lived during the late Triassic, approximately 210 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 210 millones de años, durante el Noriense, que habitó en lo que es hoy África.

facts.statement: Blikanasaurus lived from the Norian to the Rhaetian stages, between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: It has been suggested that Blikanasaurus might be a synonym of Euskelosaurus.
facts.quote: Se ha sugerido que podría ser sinónimo de Euskelosaurus.

rejected.statement: The robust hindlimb anatomy suggests that Blikanasaurus was thickly set and robust.
rejected.quote: This suggests that Blikanasaurus was thickly set and robust.
